BiblicalUsage: The word names an ambush, men lying in wait to strike, and it appears in the wars of Israel and in the psalm of the wicked. Joshua sent men to lie in ambush between Bethel and Ai, and Jeroboam set an ambush behind Judah so the battle was before and behind them. The psalm says the wicked sits in the lurking places of the villages and murders the innocent in secret.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the ambush is the picture of sin's way of working: it waits in secret and strikes where we are not looking. I hold that God sees the lurking places as clearly as the open field, and no ambush laid against His people escapes His eye.
